Docs/Replay/Guide

Replay

Replay starter

1 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓

This is a separate optional starter for the experimental godot:replay library. It does not replace the addon's ordinary Hello template or the Kit framework. Copy this directory's contents into a new project root containing the installed addons/odin_godot folder. The project includes its scene and pure gameplay model.

Build with the packaged helpers:

Shell
ODIN_GODOT_ROOT="$PWD/addons/odin_godot" SKIP_CORE=1 \
bash addons/odin_godot/build/build_scripts.sh .

Open the project in Godot and run main.tscn. Arrows move; Space takes the center coin when close enough. The coin and both bags belong to one World, the value that holds mutable simulation state. A step transfers the coin atomically. The same model runs offline or with a server:

Shell
# Separate terminals, native ENet on the same machine:
REPLAY_STARTER_ROLE=host godot --path .
REPLAY_STARTER_ROLE=client godot --path .
REPLAY_STARTER_ROLE=observer godot --path .

godot above is your Godot executable. Default role is solo, port 49480 and address 127.0.0.1; override REPLAY_STARTER_PORT / REPLAY_STARTER_ADDRESS for other native setups. These commands are a local networking example, not a public matchmaking/NAT solution. Browser exports run the default offline model; networked browser deployment requires an RTC/Party configuration supplied by your game.

Edit shared/game/game.odin for simulation rules. It has no Godot objects or I/O. scripts/starter.odin owns Session, samples input, and displays frames: retained copies of the World at individual ticks. Keep scene effects outside the simulation. The starter consumes occurrence notifications without playing irreversible effects. When adding effects, use occurrence IDs to revise or cancel them if prediction changes.

Build artifacts and generated scripts remain in your project, not in the addon. The installed addons/odin_godot/docs/replay.md guide describes the model, supported envelopes and more advanced components. The project is intentionally small; it does not claim host migration, persistence or competitive rollback merely because those library packages are present.
